subject: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

All — sharing updated drafts for Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms aligned to the tiered SLO/error budget program.

Attachments:
- Tiered_SLO_to_SLA_Mapping_Dedicated_v6.docx
- Dedicated_Customer_Comms_Draft_v3.docx

What I need today:
1) Neha/Sean: confirm we’re comfortable with the measurement language + exclusions (esp. streaming disconnect classification + fallbacks).
2) CS/SE: feedback on customer-facing framing and the “what will you see in reporting” section.
3) Hosted PM (Nikhil): sanity check we’re not creating cross-tier confusion (Dedicated vs Hosted wording).

Key changes since v5:
- Explicitly separates internal SLO targets (engineering) vs contractual SLA (credits + definitions).
- Adds a short “How we measure” appendix (request success rate vs. invalid requests/rate limits/client aborts).
- Clarifies that routing fallback is a mitigation mechanism; SLI accounting is based on what the customer experiences (i.e., final response status + end-to-end latency).

Proposed customer comms plan (Dedicated only for now):
- Email to Dedicated admins + posted in Console (banner + link to docs) the week we flip dashboards on.
- Includes escalation expectations: what data to provide, and response times during incidents.

If we can land this by EOW, I’ll route through Legal for final review and prep the outbound list w/ CS.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director of Product Management, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

Reviewed comms draft (v3) from the Enterprise CS lens.

What’s working:
- Love the separation of “SLO reporting” vs “SLA credits.” Customers mix these constantly.
- The “what doesn’t count” bullets are clear.

Edits/requests:
1) Add a very explicit line: "This does not change your current contract unless you have an executed amendment." We’ve had customers assume anything emailed is contractual.
2) The escalation section should include a simple intake checklist (timestamp/region/model/request IDs). Otherwise we get back-and-forth.
3) On incident comms: we should avoid promising a fixed cadence in this email. Better: "We will provide regular updates via status page/email as appropriate" + link to our process.

If you want, we can also include a one-paragraph "What to expect during elevated load" explanation (we may shed excess traffic vs queue indefinitely, and Dedicated gets isolated capacity per contract).

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Success (Enterprise)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:28 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

+1 to Rachel’s notes.

Two SE-specific callouts (based on recent “streaming disconnects” questions):
- We need a short FAQ snippet defining “client abort” vs “server disconnect.” Customers see a broken stream and assume it always counts against us. If we’re going to exclude client aborts, we should provide how they can confirm (e.g., SDK error codes / TCP reset vs cancel).
- The mapping doc uses “successful request” language. For streaming, some customers will ask: is a partial stream “success”? Suggest we define success as: stream completes normally and we emit a final completion event (or equivalent). Anything else is counted as failure unless it’s a client cancel.

Also: I recommend we do a 15-min enablement with Solutions Eng + CS the day before the email goes out. Otherwise field teams will get pulled into long debates.

Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions Engineering

From: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

On measurement/exclusions:

- The “doesn’t count” list in v6 is broadly aligned with the SLI spec we’re implementing.
- One nuance: retries/fallback. We should avoid saying "fallback does not count as an error." What matters is the customer-visible outcome. If we fail over and return a valid response, it’s a success for availability SLI; latency SLI is still end-to-end. If we fail over but still 5xx, it’s a failure.
- For streaming: we can commit to counting “server-side stream termination” as a failure event. Client cancels are excluded (we’ll key off cancel event + connection close pattern).

I can add a short “Streaming SLI semantics” paragraph for Elliot to fold into docs.

Aisha
Aisha Bello
Senior SRE (SLO/Error Budgets)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 12:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

Approved in principle.

Two requested edits before this goes to Legal / external:
1) In the SLA mapping doc, replace “we guarantee p99 latency” type language (even if it’s in a table header). Use “SLO reporting includes p50/p95/p99 latency; SLA is availability-based (unless contract says otherwise).” We’ve been burned by customers screenshotting internal targets.
2) Add a one-liner on error budget status: “Used internally to guide mitigation and release safety; not a contractual threshold.” (At least for this phase.)

Otherwise, this is the right direction and will reduce ambiguity in escalations.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 12:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

Agree with Sean.

One additional change: in customer comms, please avoid “Dedicated is always prioritized over Hosted” language. During constrained fleet events, we have prioritization policies, but we should not over-promise in a generic email.

Suggested phrasing:
- “Dedicated provides reserved capacity and stronger isolation than Hosted.”
- “In rare fleet-wide incidents, we may take actions (traffic shaping, failover) to protect overall service while meeting tier commitments.”

Also, in the appendix, call out planned maintenance handling and how we communicate it (scheduled notices). Legal will ask.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability

Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 1:21 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

All good from Hosted side.

One nit: In the comms draft, the section “How to interpret your dashboard” should explicitly label “Dedicated (reserved)” vs “Hosted (shared)” to prevent folks with both from mixing metrics.

Also: please avoid reusing the phrase “availability SLO” in the customer email. Call it “availability reporting” and keep “SLO” in the doc link.

Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Director of Product Management, Hosted API

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 3:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLA mapping + customer comms plan (tiered SLO rollout)

Thanks all — super helpful.

Plan:
- I’ll revise v6/v3 with:
  - Explicit non-contract change line (Rachel)
  - Intake checklist link (Rachel) + remove any implied comms cadence
  - Streaming FAQ snippet (Markus/Aisha) w/ clear “success” definition and client abort guidance
  - Remove/soften any “guarantee latency” phrasing; keep latency percentiles as reporting-only (Sean)
  - Add the error budget note (internal control, not contractual) (Sean)
  - Remove “prioritized over Hosted” phrasing; use “reserved capacity/isolation” language + planned maintenance section (Neha)
  - Tighten tier labeling and reduce SLO jargon in the email (Nikhil)

Elliot — can you help by turning the streaming + exclusions paragraph into a doc-ready FAQ block? I’ll paste into the shared drive doc tonight.

Next step: I’ll re-send as v7/v4 tomorrow AM and then route to Legal + CS enablement scheduling.

Lauren

Attachment (new): SLO_FAQ_streaming_disconnects_notes.txt
